# M4 background-noise measurement (issue #57)

Owner's observation: "вот, похоже что он иногда добавляет окружение, некоторые
семплы шумные, как фоновый звук" — some generated clips seem to carry an
audible background/ambience that others don't. For an audiobook stitched from
hundreds of independently generated segments, an *inconsistent* background is
worse than a constant one: it will pop in and out at every splice.

**Scope**: measurement only, on clips already generated by prior M4 work. No
new audio was generated for this task (a parallel agent held the GPU at the
time). Analysis reuses `docs/research/audiobook/m4_prosody_metrics.py`
(`read_wav`, `energy_db`) unchanged, extended by
`docs/research/audiobook/m4_bgnoise_metrics.py` (numpy/scipy only — no
librosa/parselmouth, per `.venv-tts`'s actual install).

## Method

For each clip: find non-speech (pause) regions with the same 20ms-frame /
-40dB-relative-to-peak / ≥150ms convention `m4_prosody_metrics.detect_pauses`
already uses. From those regions only (not "quiet" in general):

- `silence_energy_db` — median dB of the pause samples. Direct proxy for
  background level.
- `speech_energy_db` — median of the top-50%-energy frames (voice-active
  estimate).
- `snr_db` = speech − silence.
- Spectral shape of the concatenated pause audio via a **single** FFT:
  `spectral_flatness` (→0 tonal, →1 broadband), `dominant_freq_hz` +
  `dominant_freq_prominence_db`, and `broadband_energy_ratio_above_4k`.

**Fallback caveat (read this before the numbers)**: 19 of the 72 clips have no
pause ≥150ms at all — mostly the 3-second `04_stress` single-word test clips
(mean duration of fallback clips: 3.2s vs 8.2s for clips with a real pause).
For those, the script falls back to the quietest 10% of frames as a rough
floor estimate, flagged `used_fallback_floor=true`. That fallback can pick up
soft trailing speech, not real silence, so its readings are **not** trustworthy
evidence of background noise — they are reported for completeness but
excluded from the headline "how many clips are noisy" answer below.

Material analyzed (72 clips, all that existed at run time):

- `output/m4_tags/**/*.wav` — 65 clips across `00_neutral` (1), `01_emotion`
  (22), `02_prosody` (11), `03_style` (4), `04_stress` (22), `05_final_intonation` (5)
- `output/m4t0_*.wav` — 5 sentiment-baseline clips
- `output/m4_boundary_check/*.wav` — 2 clips
- `output/m4_tag_catalog/` did **not** exist yet when this ran (the parallel
  tag-catalog agent hadn't finished) — not included. If it lands later,
  re-running `m4_bgnoise_metrics.py` over it is a 5-minute follow-up, same
  method, no GPU needed.

Full JSON is not committed (regenerate on demand with the command below); this
document reports the derived summary and named examples.

```
source .venv-tts/bin/activate
python3 docs/research/audiobook/m4_bgnoise_metrics.py \
  $(find output/m4_tags output/m4_boundary_check -name '*.wav') output/m4t0_*.wav
```

## Results

### Clips with a genuinely detected pause (n=53/72 — trustworthy readings)

| stat | value |
|---|---|
| `silence_energy_db` range | −120.0 dB (digital silence) to −53.1 dB |
| mean / median / population-std | −77.2 / −74.3 / 17.6 dB |
| clips at the −120 dB floor (no measurable pause energy at all) | 4/53 |

Histogram (10 dB buckets, `silence_energy_db`):

```
-125..-115  ████               4
-115..-105  █                  1
-105.. -95  ███                3
 -95.. -85  ███                3
 -85.. -75  ██████████████    14
 -75.. -65  █████████████████ 17
 -65.. -55  ██████             6
 -55.. -45  █████              5
```

### Fraction of clips that are noisy (Question 1)

**Threshold: `silence_energy_db > −60 dBFS` (relative to that clip's own
peak), restricted to the 53 clips with a genuine detected pause.**

Rationale for −60 dB: the bulk of clean clips cluster at −85 to −65 dB or drop
to the −120 dB numerical floor (true digital silence — this is synthetic
audio, not a microphone recording, so a perfectly clean pause really can be
silence to the last bit). A handful of clips sit 15–35 dB *above* that cluster,
between −65 and −53 dB. That's the population −60 dB splits: below it is
consistent with the "clean" majority, above it is the elevated tail.

- **9 / 53 (17%)** of reliably-measured clips exceed −60 dB.
- **0 / 53 (0%)** exceed −50 dB — none of the trustworthy clips are what a
  listener would call "loud" background; the concern is a quiet-but-present
  floor, not audible hiss/rumble.
- If the 19 fallback-measured (short, no-real-pause) clips are counted too
  using their unreliable estimate, the naive fraction rises to 21/72 (29%) —
  **do not use this number**; it is inflated by the measurement artifact
  described above, not by confirmed extra noise.

**Noisiest clips (real pause, descending)**:

| silence dB | file |
|---|---|
| −53.1 | `output/m4_tags/00_neutral/neutral_baseline.wav` (and its 3 `zz_neutral_baseline.wav` copies in other category dirs) |
| −54.9 | `output/m4_tags/02_prosody/prosody_long_pause.wav` |
| −55.2 | `output/m4_tags/01_emotion/emotion_arousal.wav` |
| −55.6 | `output/m4_tags/05_final_intonation/boundary_2_continuing_thought.wav` |
| −59.1 | `output/m4_tags/02_prosody/prosody_expressive_high.wav` |
| −59.9 | `output/m4t0_neutral.wav` |
| −62.2 | `output/m4_tags/01_emotion/emotion_longing.wav` |
| −62.3 | `output/m4_tags/01_emotion/emotion_fear.wav` |
| −65.1 | `output/m4_tags/04_stress/stress_zamok_plus_2_lock.wav` |

**Cleanest clips (essentially digital silence)**:

`output/m4_tags/01_emotion/emotion_contemplation.wav`,
`output/m4_tags/02_prosody/prosody_pitch_low.wav`,
`output/m4_tags/02_prosody/prosody_speed_very_slow.wav`,
`output/m4_tags/04_stress/stress_stoit_plus_1_costs.wav` (all −120.0 dB, i.e.
no measurable energy in the pause at all), plus
`output/m4_tags/04_stress/stress_stoit_acute_1_costs.wav` (−109.8) and
`output/m4t0_whispering.wav` (−99.8).

Note the last one: a *whispering* clip is one of the cleanest in the whole
set, while `output/m4_tags/03_style/style_whispering.wav` (a different
whispering generation, no real pause detected — fallback estimate −33 dB, the
single worst number in the whole dataset) looks alarming. This is very likely
the fallback artifact, not a real difference: continuous whisper speech rarely
drops 40 dB below its own peak for 150ms, so the detector never finds a
"pause" and falls back to the quietest 10% of frames — which for whispered
speech is still partly voice, not silence. **Do not read `style_whispering`'s
−33 dB as confirmed background noise**; it needs a longer/pausier probe clip
to measure honestly.

### Correlation with tag or category (Question 2)

No clean, defensible correlation emerges.

- `01_emotion` (n=22, **all** with a genuine pause — the most trustworthy
  category): mean −76.4 dB, std 14.7. The noisiest tag is `emotion_arousal`
  (−55.2), but `emotion_helplessness` — arguably a similarly intense emotion —
  is one of the cleanest (−94.7). `emotion_fear` and `emotion_shame` are
  mid-elevated (−62.3, −65.9) with an unusually high dominant pause-frequency
  (~1.5–1.6 kHz, vs. 80–500 Hz for most other emotions) — a mildly interesting
  pattern, but n=3 clips on a single un-averaged FFT per clip is too thin to
  call it a finding; flagging it as a weak lead, not a conclusion.
- `02_prosody` (n=11, 1 fallback): the two noisiest are `prosody_long_pause`
  and `prosody_expressive_high` — plausibly because a longer/quieter pause
  window just gives the measurement more material to sample, not because the
  tag itself injects more noise.
- `03_style` (n=4, only 3 trustworthy): too small to conclude anything;
  see the whispering caveat above.
- `04_stress` (n=22, but 15/22 are fallback-only — mostly because these are
  short single-word test clips with no room for a 150ms pause): the 7
  trustworthy readings span the full clean range (−65 to −120 dB) with no
  pattern tied to accent-mark style.
- `05_final_intonation` (n=5, 1 fallback): unremarkable, clustered −55 to −77 dB.

Bottom line: the elevated-background clips are scattered across neutral
baseline, several unrelated emotions, and prosody tags — not concentrated in
any one tag family, and specifically **not** concentrated in `style:shouting`
or other single-tag suspects the owner's hunch pointed at. This is a genuine
negative result: **no tag or category reliably predicts which clips get a
noisier floor**, at this sample size.

### Tonal / music-like background (Question 3)

No clip shows a clear tonal, music-like residue.

- `dominant_freq_hz` across the 53 trustworthy clips ranges continuously from
  80 Hz to ~1.6 kHz with no repeated fixed frequency across clips (i.e. no
  consistent 50/60 Hz mains hum, no consistent single pitch that would suggest
  a music bed or oscillator artifact).
- `broadband_energy_ratio_above_4k` is ≤0.03 for almost every clip (two
  exceptions around 0.07–0.12, still modest) — the elevated-floor energy sits
  in the low-frequency / vocal-formant range, consistent with residual
  breath/vocal-fold energy leaking into the "pause" window, not high-frequency
  hiss or musical harmonics.
- `spectral_flatness` values are mostly low (tonal-looking), **but this is a
  known method limitation, not strong evidence**: the script takes a single
  un-averaged FFT over each clip's pause samples. A true white-noise signal
  analyzed this way (no Welch-style averaging across multiple windows) will
  also show spurious peaks purely from randomness — low flatness here does not
  reliably distinguish "actually tonal" from "just one noisy FFT snapshot."

**Answer: no clip in this batch shows convincing evidence of a music-like
tonal bed.** This neither confirms nor rules out the undocumented
`<|env:music|>` token (id 151702) as the mechanism — that requires generating
with/without the token, which is explicitly out of scope for this task (see
below).

### Spread between clips (Question 4 — the one that matters for stitching)

This is the strongest finding. Among the 53 trustworthily-measured clips,
`silence_energy_db` spans **67 dB**: from −120 dB (true digital silence — several
clips) to −53 dB. Even discounting the digital-silence floor as an artifact of
`log10(0)` clamping, the "real" clean cluster sits at −95 to −65 dB and the
elevated tail sits at −65 to −53 dB — a 15–40 dB jump for about a sixth of
clips. That gap, not any single clip's absolute loudness, is exactly what the
owner's ear would catch at a splice: some segments end in genuine silence,
others end with an audible low-level presence 20–40 dB above it, and there is
no tag or category that predicts which is which.

## Honesty notes

- All of this is measurement on synthetic pause windows using energy
  thresholding and a single FFT — not a VAD or perceptual loudness model.
  Treat dB numbers as relative/comparative, not calibrated absolute loudness.
- 19/72 clips (mostly `04_stress`, plus one each in `02_prosody`,
  `03_style`, `05_final_intonation`, `boundary_check`) had no real pause to
  measure and used a fallback proxy; their numbers are reported but excluded
  from every headline claim above.
- The noise is real for a meaningful minority of clips (17% of trustworthy
  measurements exceed −60 dB) — this is **not** a pure measurement artifact.
  But it is also **not** a majority-of-clips problem, and it does **not**
  correlate with any tag the owner could avoid — so "just don't use tag X" is
  not an available mitigation.
- The `<|env:music|>` / `<|env:noise|>` controllability question — whether the
  background is deliberately toggleable via those undocumented tokens, or
  reproducible/random at fixed seed — requires actual generation and is
  **explicitly not attempted here** (GPU was held by parallel agents; this
  task's brief forbade generation regardless). That remains open, tracked as
  follow-up work in issue #57, not resolved by this measurement pass.

## Options for the book (not implemented — owner decides)

1. **Post-processing noise reduction on rendered segments.** Spectral
   gate/denoise pass before stitching. Cheapest to try, no pipeline redesign.
   Risk: a denoiser tuned to remove a −55 dB floor can also dull legitimately
   quiet passages (whispering, `style:whispering` results above show real
   clips can be genuinely near-silent already) — needs per-segment tuning or
   a conservative threshold, and adds a processing step to every segment
   whether or not it needed it.
2. **Reject-and-regenerate segments above a noise threshold.** `src/audiobook.py`
   already has a per-segment manifest and audio validation step — this metric
   (`silence_energy_db` on detected pauses, threshold ~−60 dB per this
   measurement) plugs into that validation naturally: measure each rendered
   segment, and if it exceeds the threshold, regenerate with a different seed
   before accepting it into the manifest. Cost: extra generation time for the
   ~1-in-6 segments that fail (and no guarantee a re-roll passes on the first
   retry — needs a retry cap and a "give up, flag for manual listen" path).
   This is the most targeted fix and matches the existing architecture, but
   depends on the same fallback caveat above: very short segments may not have
   a detectable pause to validate at all, so the check is weakest exactly
   where segments are shortest.
3. **Normalize/level-match background between segments at stitch time.** E.g.
   measure each segment's pause floor and either duck it toward a common
   target or crossfade pause regions at boundaries. Cheapest engineering,
   does not require touching generation at all. Risk: it hides the
   inconsistency rather than removing it — a segment that's already elevated
   stays elevated, just less abruptly so; and any comfort-noise/leveling step
   risks becoming its own audible artifact if it's not done very carefully at
   the actual splice points.

None of these was implemented; this task was measurement only.

## Reproduction

```bash
source .venv-tts/bin/activate
python3 docs/research/audiobook/m4_bgnoise_metrics.py \
  $(find output/m4_tags output/m4_boundary_check -name '*.wav') output/m4t0_*.wav
```
